_comment: Alt text for images pulled in from Medium, keyed by local path. scripts/import-medium.mjs reads this when it rewrites tags, so a re-import keeps the descriptions. Run `node scripts/apply-alt.mjs` after editing to push changes into src/content/posts. An empty string is deliberate: those images are decorative stock photography that carries no information, and WCAG wants screen readers to skip them rather than read a description of a desk.
/blog/ai-powered-powerpoint-generation/0: Pipeline diagram comparing three transformation workflows for generating slides, from source content through to the finished deck.
Flowchart of the template path, from content JSON through template scoring and rerank, to a vision model picking the winner and assigning each piece of text to a region before the XML is written.
Flowchart of the image path, branching on whether the reference is a hand-drawn sketch or a finished slide, then building a prompt for gpt-image-2 and wrapping the result in a .pptx.
/blog/beyond-the-sandbox/01.webp: Title card: architecting sub-100ms production voice agents with Twilio WebSockets and a custom voice activity detector.
/blog/building-a-text-to-sign-language-f: Title card: building a text to sign AI for Pakistani Urdu, showing an Urdu letter mapped to a hand sign.
A hand forming one of the Urdu sign letters against a plain wall, the kind of frame the dataset was built from.
Grid of captured hand signs on a dark background, one frame per Urdu letter.
Labelled grid of the training dataset, each Urdu letter paired with its hand sign.
Contact sheet of dataset frames after segmentation, with the hands isolated against black.
The Urdu Character Image Generator running in a browser, showing generated hand signs for the letters entered.
Bar chart comparing cDCGAN against Stable Diffusion on FID score and training epochs.
Keras summary of the conditional GAN generator: a 100-dimension noise vector concatenated with a 37-class label, then upsampled through four transpose convolutions to a 128 by 128 image.
Closer view of the same generator summary, showing the transpose convolution stack and the parameter count at each layer.
PyTorch code computing the FID score between the directory of real images and the directory of generated ones.
Bar chart of FID score at 300, 800 and 1000 training epochs, ending at 93.53.
/blog/from-167-seconds-to-170ms/01.webp: Before and after panel: median response falling from 1670ms to 170ms, 85% faster without touching the model.
/blog/from-167-seconds-to-170ms/02.webp: Diagram of the three changes behind the speedup: Promise.all for concurrency, sharp for image preprocessing, and a WASM backend for the classifier.
/blog/from-167-seconds-to-170ms/03.webp: Before and after dashboard showing latency dropping from 1670ms to a 170 to 250ms band, CPU only, with no change to the model.
/blog/from-call-flows-to-autonomous-agen: Architecture diagram: Twilio telephony and LiveKit carrying real-time audio into an agent that chains speech-to-text, a language model and text-to-speech, with tool integrations alongside.
Diagram of the agent loop cycling through perceive, reason, plan, act and observe, with branches out to CRM, scheduling, SMS and outbound calling.
Turn pipeline running from user speech through recognition, reasoning and synthesis to playback, with the barge-in path that cancels a response mid-sentence.
Horizontal bar chart breaking one voice turn into audio capture, speech recognition, model reasoning, speech synthesis and playback.
Diagram of voice calls over Twilio and LiveKit and SMS over Twilio feeding a single agent that also places outbound calls.
/blog/how-i-optimized-vllm-for-high-conc: Grafana dashboard for the vLLM deployment: request and token throughput, average latency, KV cache usage, running requests, preemptions, and GPU and memory utilisation.
/blog/how-i-reduced-voice-ai-latency-fro: Title card: reducing voice AI latency from 1.8 seconds to under 300ms.
Low-latency voice architecture diagram beside a before and after comparison of the latency budget at each stage.
/blog/smart-privacy-shield/01.webp: The Privacy Studio screen with footage loaded and the detection panel beside it.
/blog/smart-privacy-shield/02.webp: Smart Privacy Shield landing page, headed Privacy in Motion.
/blog/smart-privacy-shield/03.webp: Testimonial section of the Smart Privacy Shield landing page.
/blog/smart-privacy-shield/04.webp: Step one of the enterprise workflow, uploading footage.
/blog/smart-privacy-shield/05.webp: Step two of the workflow, intelligent selection of the regions to protect.
/blog/smart-privacy-shield/06.webp: Step three of the workflow, automated redaction.
/projects/ai-board-scanner.webp: RF-DETR detections over a flowchart, every node and connector boxed and scored, with classes like circle, arrow and arrow_head at confidences from 0.83 to 0.97.
/projects/ai-board-scanner-arrows.webp: The reconstructed topology: each arrow traced from tail to head and matched to the pair of shapes it connects.
